messages:
sara: quick brain dump — we should consider removing the proxy-level region-affinity shim and move minimal routing decisions to the control plane. reasoning: proxy shim is getting complex (consent checks, fallback heuristics, ttl juggling) and it duplicates logic from the controller.
sara: current pain: operator teams keep debugging two code paths when a tenant falls back to another region.
devon: agree on complexity. what do we lose if proxy becomes dumb? latency jitter might increase for some cold requests.
mira: can you sketch the expected call flow?
sara: proposed flow: 1) control plane publishes a per-tenant routing hint (region, allowed-fallbacks, consent-token) to a small vectorstore (k/v). 2) proxy reads hint and caches for 5s. 3) if hint absent, proxy forwards to control plane with low-priority async fetch and uses last-known routing. 4) on fallback events controller patches hint via the same channel.
sara: example header we already use: `X-Region-Hint: eu-west-1;fallback=us-east-1;consent=required`
ian: sounds fine, but how do we handle split-brain where two controllers disagree during a control-plane partition?
devon: we should keep a safety TTL and prefer local-primary on missing/uncertain hints. that preserves availability at cost of possible residency violations — but we can gate that with enforcement flags.
mira: enforcement flags need to be auditable. propose we emit an `enforcement_reason` tag in trace/span if proxy overrides hint.
sara: agreed. also: operator UX — a single source for routing decisions reduces debugging time a lot.
alex: what about batched failovers? when controller flips 1000 tenants, proxies could be overwhelmed by pulls.
devon: controller will push a compact delta stream via our existing push-notify topic (region-routing-updates) — proxies subscribe. only a few tenants per message ideally. we need backpressure.
ops-bot: region-routing-updates subscription health: 99.98% healthy across canary proxies.
ian: important: policy testing. we need a local simulator that runs the proxy logic against recorded controller deltas. can we reuse the existing `routing-sim` harness?
mira: yes, but extend it to inject partial-controller partitions and consensus anomalies. add tests for: (a) hint drift > 30s, (b) simultaneous failover of >5% tenants, (c) consent flag flips.
sara: compatibility: plan a staged rollout — feature-flag proxies to read control-plane hints, but keep shim logic until 2 weeks after canary.
devon: ops checklist suggestion: - enable read-only mode on 10% proxies - monitor `hint-miss-rate`, `override-count`, `fallback-latency` - run synthetic residency-e2e every 15m
alex: telemetry names: `proxy.hint_miss`, `proxy.hint_override.enforcement_reason`, `proxy.fallback.count`
ian: telemetry should also tag `tenant_privacy_class` so legal can filter.
mira: about consent: if tenant requires consent and controller is unreachable, should proxy fail closed (reject) or fail open (serve local primary)? we need policy per tenant.
devon: default: fail closed for `consent=required`, fail open for `consent=optional`. operator can override with `emergency_override=true` in control plane.
sara: sample config fragment for controller -> proxy publish (yaml):
```
tenant: acme-corp
region: eu-west-1
fallbacks:
  - us-east-1
consent: required
enforcement_ttl_seconds: 30
emergency_override: false
```

ian: what about secrets (consent tokens)? don't leak to logs. proxies should only carry token hashes and validate with controller for sensitive ops.
mira: note: to support on-prem/private, controller will publish via customer VPC relay only; proxies in hosted environment will subscribe to their specific VPC topics. keep relay auth per-cluster.
alex: rollback story: if we see rise in `proxy.fallback.count` by 3x, rollback to old shim behavior via a cluster-level feature flag.
sara: open questions: - what cache TTL ensures low control-plane load but still fast failover? propose 5s default, tunable per-tenant. - how to handle multi-variant models where fallback requires a quantized model? need model-compat mapping in hint.
devon: mapping idea: add `model_variant_compat: [redwood-8q, redwood-4q]` in the hint. proxy can prefer nearest compatible.
mira: ops request: expose a `dry-run` mode where proxy logs what it *would* have done had hints been active. helpful for 2-week canary.
ian: testing plan: run chaos on controller -> introduce 60s partition and assert no residency violations for `consent=required` tenants.
sara: timeline: week0 - create controller publish API + subscription; week1 - proxy read-only; week2 - canary dry-run; week3 - enable enforcement on canary; week4 - ramp to 50%; week5 - full rollout if metrics stable.
alex: I'll add a PR with the controller API spec and sample delta format.
devon: I'll add the proxy changes and simulator tests.
mira: I'll own telemetry + legal audit hooks.
ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-8321 for rollout checklist and INFRA-8322 for push topic provisioning.
sara: thanks all. leaving this thread to track followups — please drop short updates here as you land PRs.
devon: note: added initial PR draft, link: https://git.redwood/inference/pull/4892 — please review.
ian: quick :thumbsup: on the plan.
ops-bot: deploy-notify: canary proxies rolled with `hint-read-mode=true` in staging (10 proxies) at 3579991500.
